value_stream.name: Store Remodel, Renovation & Lifecycle Refurbishment Program

fields.Participants: Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-34), Store Design, Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Finance (links to VS-40), Vendor
fields.Volume: Fixtures, shelving, counters, equipment per store

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Store Design/Procurement compile the FF&E and equipment list from" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-inspect of "Procurement source via framework agreements / RFQ" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate delivery sequencing to site" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-557 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Design, Procurement & Construction Execution (PA-109.2).)
- operational: framework agreements and early order; operational: FA capture (links to VS-35)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lead-time risk**: Imported fixtures slip the schedule; mitigated by framework agreements and early order
- **Asset-registration gap**: Remodel fixtures not capitalized; mitigated by FA capture (links to VS-35)
System Touchpoints: - Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-34); import/customs (links to VS-02.2/VS-87); quality (links to VS-31); asset register (links to VS-35); capex (links to VS-40)
Time Estimate: - Aligned to schedule; ordering 4–10 weeks lead

steps.activity: Store Design/Procurement compile the FF&E and equipment list from the design package (W3477): gondola/shelving, endcaps, service counters, paint-mixing station (links to VS-09.1), cutting equipment, tool-rental fixtures (links to VS-12.2), checkout counters (links to VS-08), backroom/storage, and specialty equipment

Procurement source via framework agreements / RFQ (links to VS-03/VS-34): vendor selection, lead-time management, import/customs for specialty fixtures (links to VS-02.2/VS-87), quality inspection (links to VS-31), and alignment to the project schedule (W3480); reuse/refurbish reusable fixtures where economical

Procurement/Facilities coordinate delivery sequencing to site (links to VS-04/VS-06), staging/storage, and handoff to installation (W3485); capture assets into the fixed-asset register (links to VS-35) and manage warranty/serials

fields.Participants: Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-34), Real Estate (links to VS-20), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Project Manager (links to VS-112), Contractor

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "conduct the pre-construction kickoff" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-557 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Design, Procurement & Construction Execution (PA-109.2).)
- operational: pre-qualification and references; operational: clear contract and change control (W3556)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-capability risk**: Contractor unfamiliar with retail/live-site work; mitigated by pre-qualification and references
- **Contract-ambiguity risk**: Scope/payment disputes; mitigated by clear contract and change control (W3556)
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (links to VS-03/VS-34); legal/contract (links to VS-100.3/W402); HSE (links to VS-24); insurance (links to VS-26); capex (links to VS-40/W1820); PMO (links to VS-112)

steps.activity: Procurement/Real Estate select the general contractor / trade vendors: pre-qualification, RFQ/RFP (links to VS-03), accreditation (links to VS-34.2), references on retail-remodel work, and HSE/insurance clearance (links to VS-24/VS-26); leverage framework/master agreements across the ~30–40/year program

Legal/Real Estate negotiate and execute the contract: lump-sum vs GMP, milestone payments (links to VS-40/W1820), liquidated damages, performance retention, warranty, HSE/permits allocation (links to VS-24/W3479), insurance (links to VS-26), and termination (links to VS-100.3/W402)

Project Manager conduct the pre-construction kickoff: scope/walk-through, schedule handshake (W3480), site HSE/rules, communications, change-control protocol (links to W3556), and acceptance criteria (W3488); confirm notice-to-proceed after permits (W3479)

fields.Participants: Project Manager, Contractor, Store Manager (links to VS-07), HSE (links to VS-24), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Facilities (links to VS-20.3)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Contractor/Project Manager execute the works per the phasing plan" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "Project Manager/HSE enforce site safety on a trading store" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-schedule of "Project Manager manage schedule, quality" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-557 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Design, Procurement & Construction Execution (PA-109.2).)
- operational: phasing (W3480) and after-hours works; operational: HSE controls (links to VS-24)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Customer-disruption risk**: Noise/dust/barriers harm the trading store; mitigated by phasing (W3480) and after-hours works
- **Safety-incident risk**: Construction alongside customers/staff; mitigated by HSE controls (links to VS-24)
System Touchpoints: - PMO/PMIS (links to VS-112); HSE/incident (links to VS-24/W330); capex/payments (links to VS-40/W1820); store ops (links to VS-07.3); quality (links to VS-31)

steps.activity: Contractor/Project Manager execute the works per the phasing plan (W3480): demolition/strip-out, structural modifications, MEP (W3484), architectural finishes, fixture installation (W3485), technology (W3486), and reset (W3487); manage the live-site separation, dust/noise control, and customer/stock protection

Project Manager/HSE enforce site safety on a trading store: barriers/fencing, signage, restricted access, working-hours rules, contractor HSE compliance (links to VS-24), incident reporting (links to W330/W471), and emergency coordination with the store

Project Manager manage schedule, quality (links to VS-31), change orders (links to W3556), milestone/payment certification (links to VS-40/W1820), site coordination with store deliveries (links to VS-07.3), and status reporting (links to VS-112/W3563); resolve issues and protect the critical path

fields.Participants: Facilities/MEP (links to VS-20.3), Contractor, Project Manager, HSE (links to VS-24), Energy Manager (links to VS-108)

workflows.name: Remodel Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing & HVAC Works

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-renew of "renewable where planned" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-capture of "Facilities/MEP commission and test MEP systems" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-557 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Design, Procurement & Construction Execution (PA-109.2).)
- operational: load calc and design coordination (W3477); operational: fire-safety design and acceptance test (links to VS-22)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Capacity-miscalculation risk**: Under-sized power/HVAC for new loads; mitigated by load calc and design coordination (W3477)
- **Fire-code risk**: Sprinkler/alarm modifications fail BFP; mitigated by fire-safety design and acceptance test (links to VS-22)
System Touchpoints: - Facility/MEP (links to VS-20.3); energy (links to VS-25/VS-108); fire/security (links to VS-22/VS-23); POS/IT (links to VS-08/VS-27); asset register (links to VS-35)

steps.activity: Facilities/MEP execute electrical works: power capacity upgrade for new departments/equipment, lighting (LED retrofit/energy efficiency links to VS-25/VS-108), POS/data cabling (links to VS-08/VS-27), fire-alarm/security/CCTV (links to VS-23), and distribution; ensure code/permit compliance (links to VS-22)

Facilities/MEP execute HVAC, plumbing, sanitary, and fire-protection works: aircon/ventilation for new zones, plumbing for service areas/restrooms, fire-suppression/sprinkler modifications (links to VS-22 BFP), and water; integrate energy-efficiency and renewable where planned (links to VS-108)

Facilities/MEP commission and test MEP systems: load testing, balancing, fire-alarm/sprinkler test and BFP acceptance (links to VS-22), and energy-performance verification (links to VS-108); hand off to facilities maintenance (links to VS-20.3) and capture assets (links to VS-35)

fields.Participants: Store Design, Contractor, Marketing (links to VS-14), Space Planner (links to VS-55), Store Manager (links to VS-07)

workflows.name: Store Fixture Installation, Signage & Graphics Rollout

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "verify plumb/level/anchorage and capacity" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document the as-installed condition" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-557 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Design, Procurement & Construction Execution (PA-109.2).)
- operational: installation QA and snag management (W3488); operational: brand standards (links to VS-14)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fixture-defect risk**: Mis-aligned/unsafe fixtures delay reset; mitigated by installation QA and snag management (W3488)
- **Brand-inconsistency risk**: Signage varies from standard; mitigated by brand standards (links to VS-14)
System Touchpoints: - Marketing/brand (links to VS-14); planogram (links to VS-55); digital signage (links to VS-75); pricing/labels (links to VS-01.2); design/asset (links to VS-35)

steps.activity: Contractor/Store Design install fixtures per the fixture plan (W3477): gondola/shelving assembly and anchoring, endcaps, service counters, department fixtures, backroom storage, and specialty equipment; verify plumb/level/anchorage and capacity

Marketing/Store Design install signage and graphics: department and wayfinding signage, brand/environmental graphics (links to VS-14), price-tag/shelf-label rails (links to VS-01.2), endcap/aisle signage, digital signage (links to VS-75), and exterior/storefront signage; ensure brand standards

Store Design/Store Manager verify fixture/signage installation against the design, capture defects into the snag list (W3488), and prepare for the merchandise reset (W3487); document the as-installed condition

fields.Participants: IT (links to VS-27/VS-99), Store Design, Project Manager, Store Manager (links to VS-07), Facilities (links to VS-20.3)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scanners, mobile devices" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-test of "IT/contractor install and configure" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "technology stack, train store staff on new devices/systems" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-557 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Design, Procurement & Construction Execution (PA-109.2).)
- operational: testing and standards alignment; operational: secure sanitization (links to VS-99)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Integration risk**: New POS/devices fail to integrate; mitigated by testing and standards alignment
- **Data-disposal risk**: Retired devices leak data; mitigated by secure sanitization (links to VS-99)
System Touchpoints: - POS (links to VS-08); IT ops/security (links to VS-27); IT asset (links to VS-99); loyalty (links to VS-13); digital (links to VS-75); asset register (links to VS-35)
Time Estimate: - Within the build window; cutover 1–3 days

steps.activity: IT/Store Design plan the technology refresh: POS terminals/software (links to VS-08), RF/handheld scanners, mobile devices (links to VS-75), network/Wi-Fi, CCTV/EAS (links to VS-23), digital signage (links to VS-75), customer-facing tech (kiosks, self-checkout), and back-office systems; align to IT standards and lifecycle (links to VS-99)

IT/contractor install and configure: cabling/power (with MEP W3484), device deployment, network/security configuration (links to VS-27.3), POS/loyalty integration (links to VS-08/VS-13), and testing; ensure offline-capability (links to VS-08) and cyber-hardening (links to VS-27.3)

IT verify the technology stack, train store staff on new devices/systems (W3490), update the IT asset register (links to VS-99/VS-35), and retire/dispose of replaced devices securely (links to VS-99 sanitization); confirm cutover readiness for re-opening (W3489)

fields.Participants: Space Planner (links to VS-55), Category Manager (links to VS-01), Store Manager/Stock Associates (links to VS-07), Replenishment (links to VS-02), Marketing (links to VS-14)
fields.Volume: Full-store reset (~35K SKUs range, department by department)

workflows.name: Remodel Merchandise Reset, Restock & Planogram Implementation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "ensure the new assortment is in stock" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-capture of "capture reset defects into the snag list" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-557 (ensure controlled execution — Remodel Design, Procurement & Construction Execution (PA-109.2).)
- operational: replenishment planning and intake tracking; operational: compliance check (links to VS-55)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stockout-at-reopen risk**: New assortment not in stock for re-opening; mitigated by replenishment planning and intake tracking
- **Reset-quality risk**: Planograms not followed; mitigated by compliance check (links to VS-55.2)
System Touchpoints: - Planogram/space (links to VS-55); assortment (links to VS-01.1); replenishment (links to VS-02); pricing/labels (links to VS-01.2); clearance (links to VS-64/VS-05.3); promotions (links to VS-58/VS-14)

steps.activity: Store Manager/Space Planner execute the merchandise reset: strike displaced stock and fixtures, relocate stock to the new layout per the planogram set (W3478/W3477), restock the new planograms (links to VS-55), and clear displaced stock (links to VS-64/VS-05.3); stage by department to keep trading zones open
steps.r: Store Mgr / Stock Associates / Space Planner

steps.activity: Replenishment/Store Manager ensure the new assortment is in stock: replenishment orders (links to VS-02/W4), new-item intake (links to VS-01.1), price tags/shelf labels (links to VS-01.2/W181), and planogram-compliance check (links to VS-55.2); resolve shortages before re-opening

Space Planner/Store Manager verify planogram compliance and space-to-assortment fit (links to VS-55.2), confirm pricing/labels/promos (links to VS-01.2/VS-58/VS-14), and sign off the reset ready for re-opening (W3489); capture reset defects into the snag list (W3488)

fields.Participants: Project Manager, Store Design, Facilities (links to VS-20.3), HSE (links to VS-24), Store Manager (links to VS-07), Contractor, Quality (links to VS-31)

workflows.name: Remodel Quality, Snag List & Commissioning / Handover

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Project Manager/Quality conduct the pre-handover inspection" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-inspect of "Contractor/Project Manager close the snag list" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-update of "Project Manager conduct formal commissioning/handover to Store Operations" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: snag discipline and retention; operational: handover documentation (links to VS-35/W3560)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Premature-handover risk**: Re-opening with open snags harms experience; mitigated by snag discipline and retention
- **Documentation-gap risk**: Missing as-built/warranty causes future maintenance issues; mitigated by handover documentation (links to VS-35/W3560)
System Touchpoints: - Quality (links to VS-31); HSE/fire (links to VS-24/VS-22); facility (links to VS-20.3); asset register (links to VS-35); capex closure (links to VS-40/W1828); PMO (links to VS-112)

steps.activity: Project Manager/Quality conduct the pre-handover inspection: structural/MEP (W3484), fixtures (W3485), technology (W3486), reset (W3487), cleanliness, and HSE/fire-safety (links to VS-24/VS-22 BFP); compile the snag/defect list and assign owners and due dates

Contractor/Project Manager close the snag list: defect rectification, re-test, and verification; manage retention/release per contract (W3482); confirm all permits/inspections closed (links to VS-22/W3479)

Project Manager conduct formal commissioning/handover to Store Operations (links to VS-07) and Facilities maintenance (links to VS-20.3): as-built drawings, O&M manuals, warranties (W3481/W3484), asset register update (links to VS-35/W3560), capex closure (links to VS-40/W1828), and lessons capture (W3494)
